what_its_for: Amlodipine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and chest pain (angina). Lowering blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It works by relaxing your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard.
how_to_take: Take amlodipine by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 5 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose to 10 mg once daily if needed. For children ages 6 to 17, the typical dose is 2.5 mg to 5 mg once daily. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store amlodipine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice or eating grapefruit while taking amlodipine, as it can increase the amount of medicine in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Be careful when standing up quickly, as this medicine can cause dizziness. Avoid driving or doing activities that require alertness until you know how this medicine affects you. Limit alcohol, as it can lower blood pressure further and worsen dizziness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe dizziness or fainting, chest pain that is new or getting worse, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, very fast or irregular heartbeat, severe swelling in your hands, ankles, or feet, or yellowing of your skin or eyes. Also call your doctor if you experience bothersome side effects such as flushing, headache, or unusual tiredness that does not go away.
when_it_works: Amlodipine starts working within a few hours of your first dose, but it may take 1 to 2 weeks of regular use before you feel the full benefit for blood pressure. For chest pain relief, it may work more quickly. Even if you feel fine, keep taking this medicine every day — high blood pressure often has no symptoms, and stopping suddenly can be dangerous.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older) may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects and are at higher risk for dizziness and falls — use extra caution when standing up. People with liver disease may need a lower dose, so tell your doctor about any liver problems. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this medicine, as it may not be safe for the baby. Children under 6 years old should not use this medication.
